It was founded in 1923 by employees of the [[Grivița]] workshops as the ''Asociația Culturală și Sportivă [[Căile Ferate Române|CFR]]'' ({{lit|CFR Cultural and Sports Association}}). Domestically, Rapid București is one of the most successful clubs in the country, having won three national titles, 13 [[Cupa României]], and four [[Supercupa României]]. Internationally, its highest achievements are reaching the quarter-finals of the [[1972–73 European Cup Winners' Cup|1972–73]] [[Cup Winners' Cup]] and the [[2005–06 UEFA Cup]], and the final of the [[1940 Mitropa Cup]]—the latter not being played because of [[World War II]]. Recently, the club was declared bankrupt in 2016, but was refounded and managed to return to the top flight in 2021. From 1939, Rapid played its home matches in burgundy and white [[Kit (association football)|kits]] at the [[Stadionul Giulești-Valentin Stănescu (1939)|Valentin Stănescu Stadium]], which was replaced by the new [[Superbet Arena-Giulești|Rapid-Giulești]] in 2022. The team has fierce local rivalries with [[FCSB]], [[FC Dinamo București|Dinamo București]] and [[CSA Steaua București (football)|Steaua București]], as well as with [[FC Petrolul Ploiești|Petrolul Ploiești]]."}}
